name: University of Canterbury
description:
The University of Canterbury is a public research university in Christchurch, New Zealand: a prestigious institution ranked amongst the top 300 universities worldwide according to QS official rankings.

It is also one of the most international universities in New Zealand, with more than 17,000 students from over 100 nationalities enrolled on a course. The university has built a reputation for providing exceptional support services, teaching quality and facilitating successful graduate outcomes; it is also ranked as a 5-star university for research and teaching.

What is the University of Canterbury acceptance rate for International Students?

The University of Canterbury acceptance rate is 50%.

highlights.title: Campus Life
highlights.value:
The University of Canterbury (UC) has more than 100 student clubs, and it encourages young voices to be heard via the Student Association. Significantly, the campus is smoke-free as it is a leafy green space, and students are encouraged to think about the environment. The range of dining options is vast regarding the number of places to get a meal or bite to eat and the cuisine served. Students can find everything conveniently located on campus, so there are plenty of spaces for scenic walks and outdoor activities. The university designs a variety of clubs, competitions and development programmes to give students sports options that complement their student experience.

It is proud of its history so that students can explore in-person and online exhibits for a slice of culture. There is even an art gallery on campus.

highlights.title: Overview
highlights.value: Students can seek out a wealth of information via the Central Library in the center of campus. A modern facility that offers a range of multimedia resources and essential books, the opening hours are extended during busy exam periods to help students excel academically. There are several field centers with field laboratories to support teaching and research - it even has an Mt John Observatory. The well-being of students is prioritized and catered for with a health center and the UC RecCenter allowing students to take fitness classes or use the gym. The university was founded in 1873, so there is a rich history behind the walls of the buildings.

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
The University of Canterbury provides various on-campus residence halls and resources for off-campus accommodation. Rochester and Rutherford Hall, Kirkwood Avenue Hall, Ilam Apartments and Sonoda Village are all situated in close proximity to each other on campus. This is a classic university housing option, with shared kitchens and common areas, lounges, laundry facilities and fully furnished bedrooms guaranteed. It is best to check with the individual residence hall regarding catering requirements, as some of the residence halls are self-catered.

The university also provides resources for house hunters via the UC Accommodation Service. Students can read a database of rental properties available in the surrounding area or check out UC's partnerships with various private accommodation providers, including Campus Living Villages. International students often opt for the Homestay program, where they can stay with a local, trusted family who can provide them with cultural experiences and meals.

highlights.title: City Life
highlights.value: Located in the heart of Christchurch, students have plenty of opportunities to develop a bustling social life while studying at the university. Lakes, mountains and forests surround the area, so the city’s residents often take up outdoor activities, and there is a social media group suggesting upcoming events for students to attend. Christchurch has received investment, with much public art, cultural events and innovative community projects occurring daily. Students feel connected to a city where something interesting is happening, the food tastes great, the bars are packed, and students from different walks of life surround them.
